# Load state: `jl-load-state`

What a list shows while its data comes, when there is none, and when it failed to come.

- Class `JlLoadState`, a molecule: `import { JlLoadState } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/load-state

A load state wraps what a list or a page draws from data that comes over the network. While the data
comes, it shows nothing for 300 milliseconds (a quick answer should not flash), then a skeleton shaped like the
content: rows, cards or lines. Then it shows the content (the default slot), the empty state of slot empty when
there is nothing, or, when loading failed, what failed and Try again, in place of the content.

load() does the work: it fetches, draws, and moves between the states; Try again runs the same load again. A later
load(), such as a live update, keeps what is shown until the new data is there, and keeps it if that load fails:
it resolves false, for the page to say so in a toast. Or set state yourself. See the Loading, empty and errors
pattern.

## Use

```ts
import { JlLoadState } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlLoadState
  count={3}
  delay={0}
  errorHeading="This could not be loaded"
  skeleton="rows"
  state="loading"
>
  <p class="muted" style="padding: 16px">The data, once loaded.</p>
</JlLoadState>
```

```html
<jl-load-state
  count="3"
  delay="0"
  error-heading="This could not be loaded"
  skeleton="rows"
  state="loading"
>
  <p class="muted" style="padding: 16px">The data, once loaded.</p>
</jl-load-state>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `state` (attribute `state`): `'loading' | 'ready' | 'empty' | 'error'`, default `'loading'`. What it shows: the skeleton, the content, the empty slot, or the error.
- `skeleton` (attribute `skeleton`): `'rows' | 'cards' | 'lines'`, default `'rows'`. The shape of the skeleton; slot loading takes one of your own.
- `count` (attribute `count`): `number`, default `3`. How many rows, cards or lines the skeleton has.
- `delay` (attribute `delay`): `number`, default `300`. Milliseconds before the skeleton shows.
- `errorHeading` (attribute `error-heading`): `string`, default `''`. What failed: "The orders could not be loaded". Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.
- `errorText` (attribute `error-text`): `string`, default `''`. The sentence under it. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.
- `retryLabel` (attribute `retry-label`): `string`, default `''`. The button that loads again. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `retry` (`onRetry` in JSX), detail `undefined`: Try again was pressed; the last load runs again.
- `state` (`onState` in JSX), detail `'loading' | 'ready' | 'empty' | 'error'`: The state changed: the data came, there was none, or it failed.

## Slots

- The default slot: The content, once loaded.
- `empty`: What it shows when there is nothing: a jl-empty.
- `loading`: A skeleton of your own, in place of the rows, cards or lines.

## Methods

- `load<Value>(task: { fetch(): Promise<Value>; draw(value: Value): void; isEmpty?(value: Value): boolean }): Promise<boolean>`: Fetches, draws, and shows the right state: the skeleton the first time and after a failure, the content or the empty slot after. Resolves whether it worked. Only a fetch that fails is a load that failed: what draw or isEmpty throws shows the error state and is thrown on, a mistake in the page that its console should show.
- `JlLoadState.whenSettled(root: ParentNode, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>`: Static: resolves once every load state under the root that can be seen, in shadow roots too, has left loading, those drawn meanwhile included; or once the signal aborts. A page that shows only once it has its data waits for it, as jl-page-outlet does.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The wrapper of every state.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Loading, then ready

Loads, then shows the rows. "Load again" keeps the rows while it reloads.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-load-state class="demo-rows">
    <div style="border: 1px solid var(--jl-line); border-radius: var(--jl-radius)">
    <jl-list-item heading="Refund request from Léa Dubois" description="Answer support emails" meta="3 days ago"></jl-list-item>
    <jl-list-item heading="Reply to Maria Rossi" description="Answer support emails" meta="3 days ago"></jl-list-item>
    </div>
  </jl-load-state>
  <div><jl-button class="demo-reload" icon="refresh" label="Load again"></jl-button></div>
</div>
```

```js
const state = root.querySelector('.demo-rows');
const load = () => state.load({ fetch: () => api.reviews(), draw: (reviews) => drawRows(reviews) });
load();
root.querySelector('.demo-reload').events.register('press', load);
```

### Failed

The request fails: what failed, in place of the list, and Try again (which fails again here).

```html
<jl-load-state class="demo-fails narrow" error-heading="The reviews could not be loaded"></jl-load-state>
```

```js
root.querySelector('.demo-fails').load({ fetch: () => api.reviews(), draw: drawRows });
```

### Empty

Nothing to show: the empty slot, with what would be there and how it gets there.

```html
<jl-load-state state="empty" class="narrow">
  <jl-empty slot="empty" icon="inbox" heading="You are all caught up" description="New reviews show up here as workflows send them."></jl-empty>
</jl-load-state>
```

### Cards

skeleton="cards", for a grid; it stays in the loading state.

```html
<jl-load-state skeleton="cards" count="3" delay="0"></jl-load-state>
```
